title: Willie Gilders's band at the Alamo, Exchange Alley and Caliente
summary: French worked about three and a half years with Willie Gilders at the Alamo and Exchange Alley with Sidney Carrere, Earl Foster and Charlie Hampton, then at Caliente.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Can you tell us about any other bands then that you joined, worked with regularly?
Well I worked with, well I worked on that up on the Alamo, you remember the Alamo.
You know I'm trying to think, I don't think I ever.
Well that's where Willie Gilders was working, it was a sort of jitney dance.
Where was that now? On the Canal and, Canal and. The Rondelet, was that the one along in there someplace?
No it was down Drys, the Continuations of Drys. Oh down that far.
Right over Macquarie, that was Tennessee Stowe.
Oh yeah. It was Canal and not Bourbon, I think it was Burgundy. On the downtown side. On the downtown side.
Cause there was another one up on the uptown side.
Yeah well I worked there three and a half years with Willie Gilders.
That's near where the Budweiser was. Yeah where the Budweiser was.

I knew that place. Well after we left there then we moved to Exchange Alley. And I was still working with Willie Gilders. I worked with Willie Gilders about three and a half years. And Poissy Alfre, you know Poissy Alfre? Oh yes. Yeah I worked with Poissy. Poissy was there. And Sidney Carrere, that's the one you don't hear them talk about. No. Sidney Carrere, he's a fine tenor man, he had a brother, Professor Carrere. I think they both passed. I think so too. I never did meet either of them. Yeah well Sidney Carrere was our tenor player. Earl Foster, you know Earl Foster. Oh yes. Yeah well Earl Foster played in the band. And we had Kato, and after Kato we had Charlie Hampton to play. Charlie Hampton played piano with us. Now Charlie Hampton played piano and banjo. That's when you talk of Charlie. He's a very good piano player, a very good banjo player. And I worked, well we worked at Alamo for I'd say about three and a half years. And after I left Alamo, well then I started working around at Caliente. You might remember Caliente. No.
Caliente was on Bienville and Burgundy. You know where the Virginia kitchen? Yeah. Right across from the Virginia kitchen there. I worked at the Caliente. And I worked a lot of spot jobs.
Yeah there was one place I think I know that was called the Magnolia for a while. It was the Magnolia Room.
Yeah. The Magnolia Room. That was the Caliente.
And Paul Barber was working there one summer about fifteen years ago. That's right. That's right.
Well, well, we worked a lot of jobs, a lot of pigments and what not. But the…
